Can you describe the appearance of the chest skin lesion, including any changes in size, color, or texture?  
Have you noticed any pain, itching, or bleeding from the lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent changes in weight, appetite, or night sweats? Additionally, do you have a family history of skin cancer or other malignancies?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin lesion on the chest. I also have Lesion has increased in size, Not painful, Not itchy.

speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me if you have had any recent sun exposure or if the lesion has become raised or scaly. REQUEST TEST: Dermoscopy of chest lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The patient reports recent intermittent sun exposure. The lesion has become more raised and rough to the touch (scaly). Dermoscopy reveals an atypical pigmented lesion with irregular borders, color variegation, and increased diameter, consistent with the clinical suspicion of melanoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Melanoma of the chest.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide high-resolution clinical photographs of the chest lesion documenting its current size, border irregularity, and color variegation.
